Six collections, one idea: things that last

Every physical line is a finished, handmade product sourced directly from small workshops — no mass-produced blanks, no faux substitutes. Our print lines pair restored public-domain artwork with made-to-order digital files.

永生花 · 黄杨花环

Preserved Botanicals

Wreaths and arrangements made from real boxwood, hydrangea and seasonal botanicals, preserved at peak freshness so they keep their color and texture for years — with no water and no wilting. Our partner workshop in Liaoning, China has supplied U.S. national retail chains since 2025.

Handcrafted Leather

Coin purses, key fobs and small carry goods cut from full-grain leather and saddle-stitched by hand in small Chinese workshops. Each piece is a finished artisan product — the leather softens and deepens in color the longer it is carried.

Ceramic Mini Vases

Palm-sized ceramic vases with a magnetic back, hand-painted one by one. Each tiny vase actually holds water, so a fridge door or steel shelf can carry a real fresh sprig — a small garden where you least expect one.

Cross-Stitch Embroidery

Hoop art and framed pieces stitched entirely by hand, one cross at a time — floral bouquets and botanical motifs worked in cotton floss on Aida cloth and linen by small workshops in China. Slow craft, made to hang on a wall and be kept for years.

Vintage Map Prints

Restored antique city views as high-resolution printable files, starting with the 1879 bird's-eye view of New York — scanned from the original held by the Library of Congress and prepared at 300 DPI for prints up to 35 × 20 inches. Public-domain artwork in warm sepia tones, sized for standard frames.

From the workshop bench to Brooklyn

EverBloom Studio LLC was founded in New York in 2026 on a simple frustration: most “everlasting” home décor is plastic pretending to be a plant. We only work with the real thing — boxwood and flowers that grew in soil, leather that came from a hide, clay that was shaped and painted by hand.

Our preserved botanicals come from our partner workshop in Lingyuan, Liaoning, which has made real preserved wreaths for three years and now supplies major U.S. retailers. Our leather, ceramic and cross-stitch lines are sourced the same way: finished goods from small workshops, tested piece by piece in Brooklyn before anything is listed for sale.
